healthcareSystem: Small public hospital (Belau National Hospital) in Koror. Limited specialist services. Compact of Free Association with the US provides some healthcare connections. Serious cases evacuated to Manila or Guam.
qualityNotes: Belau National Hospital provides basic emergency and inpatient care. Limited diagnostics and no advanced specialist services. Visiting medical teams from Taiwan, Japan, and the US periodically supplement local capacity. Serious conditions require evacuation to Manila, Guam, or Hawaii.
pharmacyHours: Hospital pharmacy open during business hours. One or two private pharmacies in Koror with limited hours.
pharmacyTips: Very limited pharmacy options. Hospital pharmacy is the most reliable source. Bring ALL medications you will need. Stock is unpredictable. Staff speak English.
prescriptionRules: Prescription system exists but options are very limited. US prescriptions recognized due to Compact of Free Association. Bring your own supply of all medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled substances
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription. Keep in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter for all prescription medications. English documentation is standard. Keep in original packaging. Bring a complete supply plus extra — resupply is not guaranteed.

travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation insurance is ESSENTIAL. Evacuation to Manila or Guam can cost $20,000-60,000+. Ensure coverage includes diving injuries (decompression sickness) and water sports — diving is the primary tourist activity.

vaccinations.notes: No special vaccinations required for most travelers. Dengue fever risk exists — use insect repellent. No malaria in Palau. Ensure tetanus is up to date for coral cuts.

waterNotes: Tap water in Koror is treated and generally safe to drink. Bottled water is widely available. On remote islands, use bottled water.
foodSafetyTips: Food at hotels and established restaurants is safe. Fresh seafood is excellent. Be cautious with reef fish from unverified sources (ciguatera risk). Wash produce with safe water.
medicalTourismNote: Palau is not a medical tourism destination. Palauans needing specialist care travel to Manila, Guam, Hawaii, or Taiwan under various assistance programs.
metaDescription: Health guide for Palau. Hospital info, diving safety tips, pharmacy access, vaccination advice, and medical evacuation to Manila or Guam.

hospitals.name: Belau National Hospital
hospitals.notes: Only hospital in Palau. Basic emergency, inpatient, and outpatient services. Limited diagnostics. Has a recompression chamber for diving emergencies. English is an official language.

dentalCare.availability: Basic dental services at Belau National Hospital. Very limited private options.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is basic. No cosmetic dentistry. Bring dental emergency supplies for remote island trips.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Go to Belau National Hospital dental clinic. Limited hours — weekdays only. For serious issues, evacuation may be needed.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated crisis line. Contact Belau National Hospital: +680-488-2552
mentalHealth.internationalLine: Crisis Text Line: text HELLO to 741741 (US-based)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. One or two counselors available through the hospital.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are extremely limited. Arrange telehealth before traveling if you need ongoing support.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Palau.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Belau National Hospital has basic wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No public transport system. Taxis available. Boats to Rock Islands are not wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Diving operators may accommodate some disabilities — inquire in advance. Resorts vary widely in accessibility. Contact accommodations before booking.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited testing available at Belau National Hospital.
covidStatus.notes: Bring rapid tests if concerned. Standard precautions apply.

insuranceClaimProcess: Belau National Hospital requires payment at time of service. Cash (USD) is preferred. Some credit cards accepted. Obtain itemized receipts for insurance claims. Documentation may be basic.

commonCosts.note: Palau uses the US dollar. Costs are moderate. Payment expected at time of service. Diving-related treatments (recompression) can be very expensive.

medicalEvacuation.note: Manila is the closest major medical hub (3-hour flight). Guam has a US military hospital and is a common evacuation point. Limited flight schedules may cause delays. Diving injuries can be treated locally at the recompression chamber.

drugNameMap.note: Available at hospital pharmacy. US brands used.
